To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
maintenance therapy with the use long-term, low-dose PEGA-IFNα2a is effective to prevent HCC occurrence irrespective the IL28B SNPs, at least for subset of CHC patient.

maintenance therapy with low-dose PGE-IFNα is effective for preventing hepatocellular carcinoma occurrence in patients with hepatitis C virus infection, irrespective of the IL-28B SNP, but the initial response of serum alanine aminotransferase levels and body mass index provide a prognostic factor for determining the risk for hepatocellular carcinoma development later in life.
maintenance therapy with low dose PEG-IFNa-2a was effective for preventing HOC occurrence in CHC patients, irrespective of the IL-28B SNP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the risk of developing hepatocellular carcinoma in cases of hepatitis C treated by long-term low-dosage PEG-IFNa-2a.
the risk of hepatoma occurrence in cases of chronic hepatitis C treated by long-term, low-dose Pegasys.
the clinical efficacy of long-term maintenance therapy with low-dose IFN for the prevention of HCC occurrence in CHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
maintenance therapy with the use long-term low-doses of PEG-IFNA-2a is an effective method for preventing the development of HCC, at least in a subset of CH patients.
maintenance therapy with the use long-term low-doses PEG-IFNa-2a is an effective strategy in preventing HCC occurrence, especially for CHC patients with high BMI or high ALT levels.
maintenance therapy with low-dose PEC-IFNα2a is effective in reducing the risk for HCC in patients with CHC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the maintenance therapy with low dose PEG-IFNa-2a is a useful strategy for preventing HCC, and that the initial response of serum transaminase levels and BMI provides prognostic value of the risk of developing of HCC later in CHC patients.
maintenance therapy with low-dose PEC-IFNα for CHC is effective in preventing HCC development.

the IL28B polymorphism is not a significant factor for determining HCC development in patients treated with PEG- IFNα-2α monotherapy, and that a high BMI (>25) and a high ALT (>40 IU/l in the 6-month period after the initiation of IFN therapy) are predictive factors for the development of HCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of developing liver cancer can be reduced by maintenance therapy with long-term low-dosage PEG-IFNA-2a, irrespective of IL28B SNP status.

the initial response of serum transaminase levels and body mass index provide a prognostic indicator for the risk of developing hepatocellular carcinoma in chronic hepatitis C virus patients receiving maintenance interferon therapy.
the IL28B genotype does not appear to be a major factor in determining the efficacy of long-term, low-dose IFN therapy for the prevention of HCC in patients with chronic hepatitis C.
